title: McMoneagle remote views a submarine being built at a White Sea shipyard

tellings.quote: in 1979 he was tasked with remote viewing an impenetrable building in a shipyard off the coast of the White Sea in Russia he described a massive nuclear submarine in the works
I just interviewed actually Joseph McMongle who figured out this you know novel uh uh Russian submarine I think in 78 or 79
tellings.difference: Gives the date as 1978 or 1979, names no White Sea shipyard and tells it secondhand from an interview.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of McMoneagle remote-viewing a new Soviet submarine being built around 1979.

as_told.title: McMoneagle remote-views a novel Russian submarine

tellings.quote: um what I got was a really unique submarine
tellings.difference: Firsthand; gives confirmation as 114 days later, names it TK-089, places it north of the Arctic Circle, and mentions a report to the National Security Council and Robert Gates.
tellings.link_reason: McMoneagle's 1979 session seeing a giant Soviet submarine being built inside a building at a northern shipyard, later confirmed.

as_told.title: Remote viewing of a giant Soviet submarine (TK-089) inside a building, confirmed 114 days later
as_told.place_text: Soviet harbor north of the Arctic Circle

plain: In 1979, Joe McMoneagle, a remote viewer, meaning someone trained to describe distant places using only the mind, was asked to look at a sealed building in a Russian shipyard on the White Sea, and he described a huge new nuclear submarine being built inside. McMoneagle tells it himself: he says it was "a really unique submarine", that he called it TK-089, that his report went to the National Security Council, that Robert Gates is part of the story, and that it was confirmed 114 days later. Michels also retells it twice, once dating it to 1978 or 1979, as evidence that remote viewing works.
